title: Sell Mineral Rights in Maxbass, ND
metaTitle: Sell Mineral Rights in Maxbass, ND
metaDescription: Own minerals near Maxbass, Bottineau County? These are Bakken-flank interests tied to older, quieter production. Get a straight answer on value.
heroLead: Maxbass sits up in Bottineau County, well off the main Bakken fairway, which is exactly why so many families here assume their old mineral interest isn't worth a phone call.
intro: This far north, closer to the Turtle Mountains and the Canadian border than to Watford City, oil-and-gas activity has always been quieter and tied more to shallow conventional formations like the Spearfish and Madison than to the horizontal Bakken wells you hear about further west. That doesn't mean a Maxbass-area mineral interest is worthless, it just means it needs a different kind of look than a Mountrail County tract would.

sections.heading: What's actually under Maxbass ground
paragraphs: Bottineau County has a long, thin history of conventional oil production rather than the dense horizontal drilling seen further south and west, and Maxbass acreage sits in that quieter category. Some tracts here have older leases tied to small vertical wells that have produced modestly for decades; others have never been drilled at all despite being under lease at some point.

sections.heading: Old family leases and forgotten paperwork
paragraphs: A lot of the mineral interests around Maxbass trace back to homestead-era ownership, land that's been in the same family since the early 1900s, with a lease signed decades ago and never revisited. If you inherited a fraction like that and have no idea whether it's still under lease or producing anything, that's the most common starting point we see.

sections.heading: What we actually do before making an offer
paragraphs: We start with your legal description, whatever you have on hand, an old deed, a probate document, even just a name and a rough location, and pull the Bottineau County Recorder's file to confirm the current chain of title. From there we check the state's oil and gas well index for any historic or active permits near your section.

Only after that do we tell you what we think a fair number looks like, and we'll say plainly if a tract has no meaningful activity and isn't worth pursuing right now. We'd rather give you an honest answer than a number designed to get a signature.

faqs.question: Is my Maxbass mineral interest worth anything if it's not in the Bakken core?
faqs.answer: Sometimes, depending on whether there's older conventional production or lease activity tied to your specific tract. It's worth having us check the actual county records rather than assuming based on location alone.

faqs.question: I don't know if my family's old lease is still active. How do I find out?
faqs.answer: Send us the legal description from any deed or lease you have and we'll check the Bottineau County Recorder's records to see what's currently on file.

faqs.question: I live out of state. Can this be handled without traveling to North Dakota?
faqs.answer: Yes. We handle title work, paperwork, and notarized deeds entirely by mail and phone for owners anywhere in the country.

faqs.question: What if the Bottineau County records show a different owner than my family?
faqs.answer: That's not unusual with older interests that were never formally updated after a death or transfer. We'll walk you through what's needed to correct the record before any sale closes.
